description.narrative: This project proposes an integrated approach to foster sustainability and resilience for food security through three interrelated components

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative: 1. There is only watershed management committees in few project districts 2. None of the project sites practiced gender -responsive- & age-sensitive decision-support tools and participatory processes for INRM in food production 3. There are 55 SHG engaged only in saving and credit services 4. Out of the projects 12 districts up to 25% has been rehabilitated 5. Less than 1% of the farmers and pastoralists utilized household solar panels 6. There is no WEB-Based GIS Embedded ES monitoring system

1. Provide hand tools and material support for beneficiary 15,000 for Landscape management activities. 2. Undertake soil and water conservation activity in 15, 000 hectare of the project landscapes. 3. Provide input to 15,000 households to increase diversified agricultural products. 4. Provide selected technologies, inputs and business development services for 100 value chain actors. 5. Develop a catalytic, upscaling and replication strategy to implement in Ethiopia after project closure ensuring the sustainability of achievements. 6. Publish project results print production and dissemination to mobilize additional resource to ILM activities. 7. Provide inputs to 600 hhs through irrigation of 150 hectares of farmland. 8. Provide agricultural inputs for agricultural diversification to 10,000 HHs and rehabilitate 5,000 hectares of farmland

1. Hand tools and material support provided to 11,573 (7,015 M & 4,558 F) beneficiaries for Landscape management activities. 2. Soil and water conservation activity undertaken in 8,924 hectares of the project landscapes. 3. Inputs provided to 17,169 (10,498 M & 6,671 F) households to increase diversified agricultural products. 4. Selected technologies, inputs and business development services provided for 1,833 (1,184 M & 649 F) value chain actors. 5. One catalytic, upscaling and replication strategy developed to implement in Ethiopia after project closure ensuring the sustainability of achievements. 6. One project result document printed and disseminated to mobilize additional resource to ILM activities. 7. Inputs to 1,834 (1,361 M & 473 F) HHs provided through irrigation of 150 hectares of farmland. 8. Agricultural inputs for agricultural diversification provided to 10,158 (5,805 M & 4,353 F) HHs and rehabilitate 5,000 hectares of farmland.

1. Strengthen multi-stakeholder and multi-scale platforms in 12 pilot sites to support integrated landscape management in food production practices. 2. Support 36 environmental school clubs and make fully functional in school compound rehabilitation and community sensitization. 3. Strengthen the gender-responsive-decision-support tool and participatory processes for INRM in food production practices in place 4. 30,000 ha with improved soil and water management that also enhances biodiversity to reach 76% of the project area benefited from ILM practice 5. 30,000 ha under diversified production system and 2500 ha of Agro-pastoral systems under integrated land management practice to reach 76% of the project benefited from diversified production system 6. 60,000 households with increased access to food through enhanced production and livelihoods diversification including off-farm activities 7. Follow up and support the 12 gender-responsive systems/ initiatives prepared to monitor multi-scale ecosystem resilience, food security and GEBs at national and landscape levels 8. Put in place Eight value chain development incentive mechanisms/infrastructure including fruit and vegetable store, ground nut processing machines 9. Invest at least USD 2 ,000 for Integrated and Sustainable Landscape Management system at 12 project woredas
